title: Proof
body_md:
Use the disk action $G_X$ from \eqref{eq:diskaction}.
The sectorwise derivative-zero bound is
\cite[Proposition~3.1, equation~(3.3)]{FLPSballs}.
Here $j'_{m,k}$ is the $k$th derivative zero in angular order $m$,
with the convention $j'_{0,1}=0$ of Section~2 of that paper.
For $0\le m\le X$ it gives
\[
 \#\left\{k\ge1:j'_{m,k}\le X\right\}
 \ge\left\lfloor G_X\left(m\right)+\frac34\right\rfloor.
\]
In that paper the frequency variable is $\lambda=X$, the spectral
threshold is $\lambda^2$, and the multiplicity weights are
$\kappa_{2,0}=1$ and $\kappa_{2,m}=2$ for $m\ge1$.
Thus its $\mathcal N_{\mathbb D}^{\mathrm N}\left(\lambda\right)$ equals
our $\mathcal N_B\left(X\right)$. Summing the sector inequalities gives
\cite[Theorem~2.3 and equations~(2.8)--(2.9)]{FLPSballs}:
\begin{equation*}
 \mathcal N_B\left(X\right)\ge\mathcal P^{\mathrm N}_2\left(X\right):=
 \left\lfloor G_X\left(0\right)+\frac34\right\rfloor
 +2\sum_{m=1}^{\left\lfloor X\right\rfloor}
       \left\lfloor G_X\left(m\right)+\frac34\right\rfloor.
\end{equation*}
The $3/4$ shift and these weights are exactly the Neumann
lattice convention of the cited paper. The spectral count includes
zero, but the lattice lower bound need not count it at very small
frequency: at $X=0$ the two sides are one and zero, respectively.
No additional zero mode is added to the displayed lower bound.
The multiplicity is two for each positive angular order and one
for order zero. We first prove the desired surplus for $X\ge20$,
then give an explicit finite bridge to $X=\sqrt{32}$.

\paragraph{The analytic range $X\ge20$.}
For $X\ge2$, \cite[Theorem~2.7, equations~(2.3)--(2.4), and
Section~2.2]{GMWZ} imply
\[
 \mathcal N_B\left(X\right)\ge\frac{X^2}{4}+\mathcal R\left(X\right),
\]
where, whenever $0<\sigma<\pi/2$ and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:diskanalyt_sigma}
 X\ge\frac{\pi}{4\left(\sin\sigma-\sigma\cos\sigma\right)},
\end{equation}
one has
\begin{equation*}
 \mathcal R\left(X\right)>
 \left(A\cos\sigma-C-\frac1\pi\right)X
 -\frac34+\frac{\cos\sigma}{4\pi},
\end{equation*}
with
\[
 A=\frac{24\pi-7\sqrt2}{8\left(4\pi-\sqrt2\right)},\,\,\,
 C=\frac{8\pi-3\sqrt2}{8\left(4\pi-\sqrt2\right)}.
\]
Notice that $A=C+1/2$ and $0<C<1/4$.
Choose $\sigma=1/2$. This value balances a positive linear remainder
with a simple Taylor bound on its admissible frequency threshold. The
choice is sufficient to start the analytic range at $X=20$; neither
$\sigma$ nor that endpoint is asserted to be optimal. Since
\[
 \sin\left(1/2\right)-\tfrac12\cos\left(1/2\right)
 =\int_0^{1/2}t\sin t\,\,\mathrm d t
 \ge\int_0^{1/2}\left(t^2-t^4/6\right)\,\,\mathrm d t=\frac{13}{320},
\]
the bound $\pi<22/7$ implies that the threshold in
\eqref{eq:diskanalyt_sigma} is less than $1760/91<20$.
Moreover, $\cos\left(1/2\right)\ge7/8$ and $\pi>25/8$ give
\begin{align*}
 A\cos\left(1/2\right)-C-\frac1\pi
 &=\frac12\cos\left(1/2\right)-C\left(1-\cos\left(1/2\right)\right)-\frac1\pi\\
 &>\frac7{16}-\frac1{32}-\frac8{25}=\frac{69}{800}.
\end{align*}
Also $\cos\left(1/2\right)/\left(4\pi\right)>49/704$. Thus, for $X\ge20$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:diskanalyt_high}
 \mathcal R\left(X\right)>
 \frac{69}{800}X-\frac34+\frac{49}{704}
 \ge\frac{3677}{3520}>1.
\end{equation}
This proves \eqref{eq:diskanalyt_surplus}, strictly, on that range.

\paragraph{A polynomial lower bound for the action.}
Set $H\left(t\right)=\sqrt{1-t^2}+t\arcsin t$ for $0\le t\le1$.
Differentiation cancels the two terms $t/\sqrt{1-t^2}$ and gives
$H'\left(t\right)=\arcsin t$. For $0\le u<1$, convexity of
$v\mapsto\left(1-v\right)^{-1/2}$ gives $\left(1-u^2\right)^{-1/2}\ge1+u^2/2$.
Hence
\[
 H'\left(t\right)=\int_0^t\frac{\,\mathrm d u}{\sqrt{1-u^2}}
 \ge t+\frac{t^3}{6}.
\]
Since $H\left(0\right)=1$, integration from zero to $t$ proves
\begin{equation*}
 H\left(t\right)\ge1+\frac{t^2}{2}+\frac{t^4}{24}.
\end{equation*}
The elementary constant bound follows from the positive integral
\[
 \frac{22}{7}-\pi
 =\int_0^1\frac{t^4\left(1-t\right)^4}{1+t^2}\,\mathrm d t>0.
\]
\paragraph{The printed finite bridge.}
The finite bridge is constructed in layers: a row with lower count $c$
covers the energy interval $\left[4k,4\left(c-1\right)\right]$, so choosing the next $k=c-1$
ensures closed overlap. The angular endpoints are chosen to make the
polynomial sign tests positive while keeping the table short. They are
not optimal eigenvalue enclosures.
In the following table, $\left(M_1,\ldots,M_s\right)$ lists the largest
angular order retained at floor level $n=1,\ldots,s$. The next
column is a vector of strict rational lower bounds
$\ell_{k,n}=d_{k,n}/1000$ for $G_{2\sqrt{k}}\left(M_n\right)+3/4$.
Thus the $n$th entry is strictly greater than $n$. These decimals
denote exact fractions, not rounded values of the action.

The identity $G_X\left(m\right)=XH\left(m/X\right)/\pi-m/2$
converts the polynomial lower bound into action estimates.
To check each bound, put $m=M_n$ and
$P=384k^2+48km^2+m^4$. The bound for $H$ above and $\pi<22/7$ give
\[
 G_{2\sqrt{k}}\left(m\right)+\frac34
 >\frac{7P}{4224k\sqrt{k}}-\frac m2+\frac34.
\]
For $d=d_{k,n}$ the right side exceeds $d/1000$ exactly when
$7000P>4224k\sqrt{k}\left(d-750+500m\right)$. Both sides are positive,
so squaring reduces this to the explicit integer test
\[
 T\left(k,m,d\right):=\left(7000P\right)^2-k\left(4224k\left(d-750+500m\right)\right)^2>0.
\]
All $94$ tests for the $22$ rows have positive integer values.
For example, $k=8$, $m=4$, $d=1018$ give $P=30976$ and
\[
 T\left(8,4,1018\right)=216832000^2-8\cdot76640256^2
            =26285506035712>0.
\]
This proves $G_{2\sqrt8}\left(4\right)+3/4>1.018>1$.
Among the $94$ integer tests the smallest value is
$T\left(8,1,2078\right)=3506047446592>0$; every other row can be checked
by the same displayed integer formula.
Because $G_X$ decreases in its angular argument, the $n$th
comparison supplies $2M_n+1$ modes at floor level $n$.
Summing these layers gives the count $c$, except for the starred
row, whose two additional modes are justified below.

For the starred row $k=11$, the phase layers supply 12 modes
and use no mode of angular order five. In that sector, take
\[
 f\left(r\right)=r^5\left(1-3r^2/4\right).
\]
Suppressing the common angular factor, direct integration gives
\[
 \int_0^1\left(f'\left(r\right)^2+25r^{-2}f\left(r\right)^2\right)r\,\,\mathrm d r
 =\frac{53}{112},\,\,\,
 \int_0^1f\left(r\right)^2r\,\,\mathrm d r=\frac{61}{5376}.
\]
The quotient is $2544/61<44$. The cosine and sine angular
factors yield two independent modes, orthogonal for both forms
to the sectors used in the phase lower count. Hence
$\mathcal N_B\left(\sqrt{44}\right)\ge14$, as claimed.

Each row yields $\mathcal N_B\left(X\right)\ge c$ throughout
$4k\le X^2\le4\left(c-1\right)$, by monotonicity in the energy. Therefore
$\mathcal N_B\left(X\right)-1\ge X^2/4$ on that closed interval. Each next value of
$k$ is exactly the preceding $c-1$, so these intervals cover
$32\le X^2\le424$. This overlaps the range $X\ge20$ proved in
\eqref{eq:diskanalyt_high}, completing the proof.
